product.name: NSCB
product.purpose: A cross-platform, Rust-owned Nintendo Switch content-file toolkit for trustworthy inspection, verification, extraction, transformation, packaging, compression, restoration, organization, and qualified local-USB device workflows. It serves CLI/TUI users and embedding Rust hosts through one typed, runtime-neutral Engine facade without bundling proprietary content.

primary_users.role: Desktop user managing supported Nintendo Switch content files
primary_users.technical_level: Comfortable with file formats and advanced content workflows; needs truthful inspection and safe, understandable results
primary_users.work_context: Inspects and organizes legally obtained NSP/XCI/NSZ/XCZ/NCA content, including split and multi-content packages, across supported desktop platforms.

primary_users.technical_level: Technical user composing unattended scripts and consuming stable typed machine output
primary_users.work_context: Runs deterministic batch inspection and processing without prompts, parses JSON/JSONL and exit classes, and needs reproducible error and outcome semantics.

primary_users.role: Developer embedding NSCB in another Rust application
primary_users.technical_level: Experienced Rust host/application developer integrating typed capabilities and controlling lifecycle and application policy
primary_users.work_context: Integrates the supported Engine directly, including in Argus ROM Toolkit, while owning configuration, persistence, execution environment, UI and output policy.

jobs_to_be_done.statement: Inspect supported content-file structure and validated identity/metadata read-only, with byte-derived format recognition and truthful errors.
Validate selected structural and cryptographic checks with clear applicability, prerequisites and integrity/authenticity semantics.
Explicitly convert, extract, split, repack, patch, compress or restore compatible content without silent content changes.
Organize or move content with deterministic names, complete Split sets, safe conflicts, byte verification and atomic publication that preserves originals on failure.
Review fully resolved immutable Operation Plans and execute noninteractive Jobs with typed terminal outcomes, durable evidence and stable machine output.
Use an explicit locally connected, user-operated Switch responder for capability-qualified installation, storage transfer, inventory and selected Dump/backup operations.
Embed NSCB through one stable typed Rust facade while the host retains lifecycle, persistence, runtime, provider and destination policy.
Deliver portable, integrity-checked binaries and auditable dependency/provider qualifications for the four declared v1 host targets.

must_reduce: Loss or corruption of original content during split, transformation, move or publication
Keeping duplicate originals because combined multi-content packages cannot safely be split
Misleading format, verification, authenticity, modification or device-success claims
Unexplained failures, hidden content changes, implicit interactive prompts and unpredictable batch behavior
Platform-specific divergence in Engine behavior or CLI automation contracts
Embedding friction from bundled standalone state, mandatory executors or leaking private implementation crates
must_not_become: An in-place port of legacy NSC_BUILDER or a public API coupled to its architecture
An unrestricted launcher for arbitrary external helpers or unqualified user-installed executables
A distribution of proprietary Nintendo keys, tickets, firmware, personal certificates or unlicensed game material
A Switch-side responder manager, remote device-administration suite or unqualified device writer
A workflow that silently patches content, overwrites original files, self-elevates, self-updates or reports unsupported success
An embedding facade that forces host adoption of standalone NSCB configuration, SQLite, user-directory storage or Tokio
A dedicated Flutter NSCB application in v1
experience_principles: Validated bytes and typed structural evidence outrank filenames, extensions and provider-native text
Read-only inspection and verification never silently mutate user content
Every content-changing operation is explicit, planned, revalidated and safely published
Success claims reflect executed applicable checks and verified postconditions, not skipped work or helper exit status
Stable typed results, machine records and error categories separate semantics from localized presentation
CLI, TUI and embedding adapters consume the same Rust-owned application capabilities
Embedded hosts own outer lifecycle, runtime, storage and product-specific policy
Only synthetic or explicitly licensed redistributable fixtures belong in the repository; provider binaries require exact-version qualification
Capabilities and release compatibility are advertised only when demonstrated on supported platforms
